xando_stickdraw.notes: Stick/Draw RPO structure and play-side linebacker conflict read.

pre_snap_keys: Identify likely man vs zone and obvious pressure.
Alert any isolated tagged route if leverage is favorable.
post_snap_guidance: Against man, crossing traffic and separation are the main answer.
Against zone, do not blindly chase a runner into coverage; work the available sit/window and flat-control elements.
Move on quickly if the first mesh runner is capped.

pressure.note: Crossers can provide fast answers, but protection and route timing still matter.

pre_snap_keys: Check middle-field structure and pressure.
Know which deeper in-breaking route is paired with the shallow.
post_snap_guidance: Use the shallow as a fast man/separation answer.
Against zone, let underneath defenders declare and work the intermediate window if the shallow is capped.

pressure.note: A shallow can become the fast outlet if it clears immediately.

pre_snap_keys: Choose/confirm the concept side and identify cloud/flat leverage.
post_snap_guidance: Common teaching is deep-to-intermediate-to-short, but exact progression is system-specific.
Key the flat/overhang defender: widening or sinking changes which layer opens.

pressure.note: Full progression can be slow versus immediate pressure unless a built-in outlet is available.

pre_snap_keys: Identify two-high/cloud looks and corner leverage.
post_snap_guidance: High-low the corner/flat player rather than pre-determining the hitch or corner.
If the defense carries/squats differently than static Cover 2, confirm leverage before throwing.

pressure.note: The underneath component can be quick, but the corner route may not have time versus pressure.

pre_snap_keys: Count deep safeties/open vs closed middle.
Check isolated outside leverage and press/off depth.
post_snap_guidance: Confirm safety rotation before committing to a seam.
Outside and inside verticals can adjust to leverage in many systems; exact tags are playbook-specific.
Against three-deep structures, seams can stress the spacing between deep-third defenders.

pressure.note: Vertical routes need time; use only if protection or an immediate leverage throw is present.

pre_snap_keys: Check press/off leverage and inside help.
Identify potential robber/hole defender.
post_snap_guidance: Confirm the throwing lane; do not throw blindly into a robber/hole player.
Versus pressure/man, favor immediate separation and leverage.

pressure.note: Quick timing can punish pressure when the throwing lane is clean.

pre_snap_keys: Take a free gift hitch if the defense concedes it.
Identify the underneath movement/conflict defender.
post_snap_guidance: If the key widens, the inside stick/window can open.
If the key squeezes/brackets inside, reset to the flat/high-low component.
Against blitz, the slot/stick can become an immediate answer in systems that teach that rule.

pressure.note: Quick-game structure often provides an immediate answer.

pre_snap_keys: Count blockers vs immediate perimeter defenders.
Check cushion and overhang leverage.
post_snap_guidance: Get the ball out immediately if the numbers/leverage remain favorable.
Abort/avoid if the defense has clearly out-leveraged the screen.

pressure.note: Can punish interior pressure if perimeter numbers are favorable.

pre_snap_keys: Count the box and locate the safety/overhang responsible for fitting the run and closing the glance window.
Check receiver leverage before treating the glance as available.
post_snap_guidance: Key the designated conflict defender; run/pass choice is tied to whether he inserts into the run fit or stays in the throwing window.
Do not assume every similarly named RPO uses the exact same read player; confirm playbook implementation.

pressure.note: Can exploit an inserting conflict defender, but an unblocked pressure player can also force a fast decision.

pre_snap_keys: Count the box and perimeter defenders.
Identify the apex/overhang who can be conflicted by run fit vs bubble responsibility.
post_snap_guidance: If the conflict defender commits into the run fit and the perimeter numbers hold, the bubble becomes available.
If he widens/holds outside leverage, stay with the run side of the read when the box remains favorable.

pressure.note: The conflict read can punish an inserting overhang, but pressure source/location matters.

pre_snap_keys: Count the box and identify extra fitters.
Prefer favorable numbers or pair with an RPO/constraint when overloaded.
post_snap_guidance: Press the designed track and react to leverage/cutback rather than bouncing automatically.

pressure.note: Pressure can create penetration or vacated space; front and box count matter more than coverage label.

pre_snap_keys: Check edge numbers and force-player alignment.
post_snap_guidance: Stretch the front and take the available lane; avoid predetermining bounce vs cutback.

pressure.note: Edge pressure/penetration can disrupt the track; alignment matters more than coverage.

pre_snap_keys: Identify front structure and likely spill/box player.
post_snap_guidance: Follow puller leverage and avoid outrunning the blocking picture.

pressure.note: Run blitzes can disrupt pull timing; front is more important than coverage shell.

pre_snap_keys: Identify the read defender and force/pitch relationship when applicable.
post_snap_guidance: Give/keep based on the read defender's commitment; do not decide solely from the pre-snap picture.

pressure.note: An aggressive edge can be manipulated if he is the read player; extra pressure elsewhere can change the equation.
